title: Faith Is the Brightest Evidence
description: Faith Is the Brightest Evidence in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 120, headed “Faith of things unseen, Heb. 11. 1 3 8 10”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Faith is the bright-est ev-i-dence Of things be-yond our sight, Breaks thro' the clouds of flesh and sense, And dwells in heav-enly light.

lines: Breaks thro' the clouds of flesh and sense,
It sets times past in present view,
Of things a thousand years ago,
By faith we know the worlds were made
He sought a city fair and high,
And faith assures us, tho' we die,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
